anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Query Plan Selection Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly : Application-level SQL or transactional logic that processes more data, rows, or time than business semantics require.
Query Plan Selection Anomaly : Optimizer chooses a substantially sub-optimal execution plan despite having reasonably accurate statistics.

When both root causes strike simultaneously, the database exhibits pronounced and erratic performance degradation: statements already bloated by poor SQL logic are executed with inefficient access paths, causing extreme elongation of response times, frequent appearance in slow-query and lock-wait logs, sudden shifts between fast and very slow executions, CPU spikes from unnecessary scans or nested-loop explosions, and inflated I/O and memory footprints that ripple through the buffer cache and temp space. As transactions stay open longer, secondary effects such as lock retention, queue buildup in connection pools, and application-level timeouts become common, obscuring which layer is primarily responsible.

Causally, verbose or improperly filtered SQL inflates row counts and widens intermediate result sets. The optimizer, already prone to picking fragile or non-robust plans, now evaluates inflated cardinality estimates and may favor full scans, Cartesian joins, or non-parallel plans that magnify the workload’s excess. Conversely, a mischosen plan that scans or joins large tables amplifies the cost of the workload logic’s unnecessary columns, predicates, or batch size, turning what would have been a minor inefficiency into a severe bottleneck. The feedback loop—sub-optimal logic feeding a sub-optimal plan—exacerbates resource consumption, stretches transaction length, and masks the individual contribution of each root cause, making diagnosis and remediation more difficult than if either anomaly occurred in isolation.

entry.official_definition: Terminates any session that has been idle, but not within an open transaction, for longer than the specified amount of time.
entry.trigger_condition: A session is idle and not inside an open transaction longer than the configured threshold.
entry.workload_impact: The session is terminated; the documentation warns about using this with connection pools or middleware.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
